title: Turtle Shell's First Cry
next_chapter_hook: Where did that gaze come from? Was it the gaze of Heaven's Eye, or was someone else watching in the shadows? Chen Ji's back was soaked with cold sweat.

text.content: The third hour after midnight, Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters. A waning moon hung like a hook, its light slicing the window lattice shadows diagonally across the floor, like silent cracks. Chen Ji sat cross-legged on a meditation cushion, the turtle shell recovered from the ruins placed before him. The shell's surface was mottled, with twisted lines faintly visible—some resembled deliberately scrambled text, others like lightning trapped within a tiny space. He had observed this object for seven days, could trace every crack with closed eyes, yet never could penetrate its mysteries. 'Mo Xiansheng said that the awakening of the Tianji Record requires the host to trigger it actively...' he murmured, fingertips unconsciously stroking the deepest groove along the shell's edge. His heartbeat was格外清晰 in the silence, as if something within him lay dormant, waiting to be awakened.

For seven days, he kept the turtle shell close to his body—disguised as an ordinary servant during the day, researching alone at night. He knew better than anyone that investigating such a thing under the sect's watchful eyes was walking a tightrope—once discovered, what awaited him would be far worse than mere expulsion. The faint glimmers occasionally emanating from the shell's surface, he had never mentioned to anyone. Occasionally in the deep night, he would hear a subtle humming from within the shell, as if something was breathing, waiting. At this moment, that humming seemed clearer than usual, as if it could sense his hesitation.

dialogue.content:
Having come this far, there was no turning back.

He took a deep breath and fiercely gripped the turtle shell in his palm. The icy sensation instantly pierced his marrow; Chen Ji instinctively wanted to release it, yet discovered his fingers were no longer under his control—the shell seemed to come alive, frantically absorbing the warmth from his palm. The patterns on the shell's surface began to tremble violently, emitting tiny crackling sounds, like undercurrents churning beneath ice. Agonizing pain exploded from his palm, racing through his meridians directly into his mind!

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth, veins bulging on his forehead. He felt his consciousness being dragged by an invisible force, like falling into an bottomless icy lake—surrounded by endless darkness and bone-piercing cold. 'Is this... the awakening of the Tianji Record?' he screamed internally, yet no sound emerged. Blurry points of light appeared in his vision—those lights gradually gathered and rotated, sketching a hazy scene—he saw himself walking along a mountain path, at dawn three hours later. In the vision, a faint smile hung at the corner of his mouth, as if confronting someone.

The预见 flickered past like a carousel: mountain path, dawn, blurry figures... then everything abruptly stopped. A crisp 'crack' sounded, and a new crack appeared on the turtle shell's surface, intertwining with the original patterns into an ominous design. The excruciating pain receded like a tide, Chen Ji collapsed trembling on the ground, gasping heavily. His head felt as if pierced by iron nails, every breath tugging at tearing agony. More terrifyingly, he felt something inside him rapidly draining away—a hard-to-describe lightness, as if the weight of life was being extracted from the depths of his soul.

'Heavenly Fate...' Chen Ji whispered tremblingly. He had heard this concept mentioned in passing by Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul, yet never imagined he would experience it firsthand. Mo Xiansheng had said that the power of the Tianji Record was not free—every time one foresaw the future, they were borrowing from Heaven. And the interest on that loan was the Heavenly Fate Value—the fundamental element representing a cultivator's luck and lifespan. He struggled to raise his palm, examining the turtle shell by moonlight—faint blood-red light glimmered within the cracks, like an unhealed wound.

dialogue.content: 'Five hours... merely seeing three hours into the future cost a full five points of Heavenly Fate?' Chen Ji gripped the turtle shell tightly, knuckles white. Mo Xiansheng had said his current Heavenly Fate was merely a few dozen points—each one precious. At this rate of consumption, he could only perform a dozen or so more visions. Worse, in that instant, he couldn't even control the timing of awakening—if he hadn't prepared by gripping the shell in advance, showing such a wretched state before everyone in the sect's main hall would have had unimaginable consequences.

text.content: The headache gradually subsided, but that feeling of being watched grew increasingly intense. Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze involuntarily drawn to the night sky beyond the window. Stars scattered, the moon hidden by thin clouds—everything seemed no different from usual. Yet in the very moment the vision descended, he clearly felt something watching him from extremely high and far above. That gaze carried no emotion, yet it made all his hair stand on end, as if an invisible ancient beast had locked onto him. It was an existence far beyond his current level of understanding—perhaps something even more terrifying than an Nascent Soul old monster.

choice.prompt: The previous awakening came too suddenly; if not for being prepared, the consequences would have been unimaginable. The next activation of the Tianji Record must be more cautious.

choices.text: Strike while the iron is hot, try again
choices.description: The body's fatigue hasn't fully subsided, but this is precisely when perception is sharpest. If we can ride this momentum to activate again, perhaps we can discern the triggering conditions.
choices.visible_cost: Heavenly Fate may be additionally consumed by 3-5 points
choices.visible_reward: May master a stable triggering method
choices.risk_hint: High risk: If Heavenly Fate drops below the critical point, may faint on the spot

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth and gripped the turtle shell again, the cold sensation from his fingertips spreading throughout his body. He closed his eyes, attempting to replicate the previous state—that feeling of actively probing consciousness into the shell. However, no matter how hard he tried, the turtle shell merely lay cold in his palm, showing no reaction whatsoever. After a moment, an even more violent dizziness struck; blood actually trickled from his nose. 'Dammit...' he cursed softly, having to release and give up. It seemed the awakening of the Tianji Record was not something one could trigger at will—it required certain specific conditions.

choices.description: Haste makes waste. The body's warnings are already obvious enough; rather than forcibly exploring, it's better to record all details of this awakening in detail, then search for patterns.

text.content: Chen Ji retrieved a scroll of yellowed bamboo from under his pillow and began recording by moonlight: awakening time, third hour after midnight; triggering method, actively gripping and concentrating; consumption, approximately five points of Heavenly Fate; side effects, headache, nosebleed, brief dizziness. He wrote each word and sentence with extreme detail, not even omitting his breathing rate at the time. At the end, he paused his brush, gazing thoughtfully at the cracks on the turtle shell.

Having finished recording, Chen Ji hid the bamboo scroll in a compartment within the wall bricks, then turned to examine the turtle shell. After repeated observation, he discovered the crack distribution wasn't without pattern—if those lines were reconnected in his mind, they faintly formed the embryonic shape of some formation. 'So that's it...' he realized with sudden clarity. The cracks on the turtle shell weren't damage, but naturally formed guiding lines—only when a cultivator's spiritual energy was injected in a specific manner could the dormant power within be activated. In other words, the triggering condition was related to spiritual energy flow, not simply dependent on will.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, recalling the trajectory of spiritual energy flow just now. It was a method of circulating power he had never attempted before, completely different from the conventional techniques passed down by the sect. He carefully adjusted his breathing, attempting to guide the only remaining spiritual energy within him along the same path. When that faint stream of warmth reached his palm, the turtle shell trembled slightly once more—but this time, he didn't recklessly delve deeper, instead withdrawing the power after a cautious taste.

text.content: 'As expected...' Chen Ji opened his eyes, a faint smile appearing at the corner of his mouth. Although he had merely gently probed just now, he had already captured the key—the spiritual energy must be injected in a counterclockwise spiral manner, while maintaining a tranquil mind. Any haste or distracting thoughts would cause the power to backfire. He silently recorded this discovery in his heart, while warily scanning his surroundings. The night watchman's wooden clapper sounded outside the Servants' Quarters; everything appeared peaceful, yet that gaze from above remained lodged in his heart, like a sword suspended overhead.

choice.prompt: Having initially mastered the method of spiritual energy guidance, truly stable use of the foresight ability still requires repeated verification. The night is still deep—how should this time be utilized?

choices.description: While memory is fresh, attempt two to three more spiritual energy guidances, gradually consolidating control over the Tianji Record. The risk is possibly consuming Heavenly Fate again.
choices.visible_cost: Heavenly Fate may decrease by 2-3 points
choices.risk_hint: Medium risk: nighttime activity may be noticed by others

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and attempted spiritual energy guidance again. This time, he deliberately controlled the amount injected, allowing that warm current to seep into the turtle shell at an even slower, steadier pace. The patterns on the shell's surface lit up with faint light once more, but far less violent than before. He felt a mild dizziness wash over him, but it quickly subsided. This time, the consumption of Heavenly Fate seemed greatly reduced—看来 '浅尝辄止' 的策略确实有效。He opened his eyes, fine beads of sweat already covering his forehead, yet a flash of excited light gleamed in his eyes.

choices.description: Having consumed quite a bit tonight, continued risks are not worth it. Better to rest and conserve energy, reconsider tomorrow. Besides, that inexplicable gaze left his heart uneasy.

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the turtle shell into his chest and lay back on the simple wooden bed. Exhaustion rushed over him like a tide; his eyelids grew impossibly heavy. However, just as consciousness was about to slip into darkness, that gaze from high above reappeared—as if something was watching him from above the firmament, watching his every thought, every breath. His eyes snapped open, yet outside the window the moon remained clear and the stars sparse—nothing unusual at all.

He simply stopped forcing himself to sleep, instead half-reclining against the headboard, letting his thoughts drift freely. Mo Xiansheng had said that every host of the Tianji Record came to a bad end—they either died from Heaven's backlash or were killed by power-hungry strong ones who coveted the treasure, without exception. Chen Ji had thought it was just fearmongering, but now it seemed the waters behind this turtle shell ran far deeper than imagined. That gaze... was it the observation of Heaven's Eye? Or was there someone else? Either way, it meant he had already been marked. From now on, he must be even more careful.

The mournful cry of a night owl echoed from outside the window, eerie and prolonged. Chen Ji closed his eyes, silently reviewing in his heart the gains from tonight: mastered the basic method of spiritual energy guidance; confirmed that Heavenly Fate consumption is proportional to foresight duration; discovered that triggering conditions relate to mindset, requiring a tranquil heart to be effective. These pieces of information seemed scattered, yet formed the cornerstone of his future plans. 'A废物 also has废物's uses...' he murmured to himself, a smile hooking at the corner of his mouth that others couldn't comprehend.

However, just as he was about to fall asleep again, a sudden wave of inexplicable palpitations struck. Chen Ji startled awake, pupils contracting sharply—he clearly felt that gaze becoming more solid, more proximate, as if something was tearing through the void, closing in on his location. It was a fear beyond language, like a tiny ant facing an overturning sky. He stared fixedly at the night sky beyond the window, blood in his entire body seeming to flow backward.

The next instant, that oppressive sensation receded like a tide, as if it had never existed. The moonlight remained cold, the night breeze gentle—everything returned to calm. Chen Ji sat stunned for a long while, his back soaked with cold sweat. He didn't know what had just happened, nor whether that gaze was a hallucination or a real threat. But one thing he could be certain of—the awakening of the Tianji Record meant far more than mere power; it was more like a key, opening a door that should never have been opened. And the things behind that door were, following the key's aura, approaching him step by step.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. Whatever that gaze was, he currently had no capital to oppose it. Rather than worry without cause, better to thoroughly digest tonight's discoveries, and calculate when he has grown stronger wings. He pressed the turtle shell against his chest, feeling that weak yet real warmth—this was his trump card, and his foundation for standing firm in this survival-of-the-fittest cultivation world. No matter how perilous the road ahead, he would not retreat. After all, he was that '废物' Chen Ji. That Chen Ji whom everyone despised, whom fate repeatedly crushed, yet who always clenched his teeth and survived.

The night deepened; only steady breathing sounds remained in the Servants' Quarters. Chen Ji finally fell into a deep sleep, clutching the turtle shell that carried all his hopes to his chest. In his dream, he saw that hazy future again—mountain path, dawn, and that blurred face. That person seemed to be saying something to him, but the voice was drowned by the wind, indistinct. The only clear thing was that meaningful smile at the corner of that person's mouth. Chen Ji awoke with a start, finding the sky outside the window already turning bright. A new day had begun, and his entanglement with the Tianji Record was just beginning.
